body:
ben: heads up — multiple APAC customers reporting very high p95 (600-900ms) and intermittent 502s this morning. they all show X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1 even though clients are in apac. filing support tickets now.

alice: on it. can you paste one request id + example curl to repro?

ben: request id 01H8kd9qT1 (2026-11-02T14:03:12Z). repro curl: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
```
response headers include `X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1` and body sometimes returns `502 backend unavailable`.

carlos: checking infra — I see a peering flap between edge-apac and core-eu around 2026-11-02T14:02:13Z. bgp session dropped ~60s then re-established. looks like routes briefly preferred eu. pulling peering logs now.

peering-bot: bgp-session edge-apac -> core-eu RESTART (60s), routes updated, as-path changed — automated alert 2026-11-02T14:02:14Z.

alice: hmm — we rolled a routing TTL change yesterday in rollout `ttl-v2-2026-11-02`. the policy that decides local vs fallback uses a TTL cache keyed to colo. if TTL got increased unintentionally, fallback preference could persist longer after peering flaps. that would explain cross-region stickiness.

dana: i ran the rollout and skipped apac canary because of noisy quotas. i didn't expect TTL semantics to influence peering selection. rollout id `ttl-v2-2026-11-02`.

alice: mitigation: applying a temporary override for affected orgs to force apac-edge: `/ops/routing/overrides apply --org acme-inc --region apac-edge` -> applied. requests for acme-inc dropped to ~40ms p95. :thumbsup:

ben: customers confirm improvement. one oddity: after we re-routed some clients back, a few requests started failing with 401 `token-region-mismatch`. looks like auth tokens are validated against a region-scoped cache and token binder expected tokens issued by the region they hit. reproducer:
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{"error":"token-region-mismatch","expected_region":"eu-west-1"}
```

carlos: that fits — sequence: (1) peering flap -> traffic moved to eu; (2) auth service cached token binding as eu; (3) when traffic moved back to apac, token validation failed because cache still had eu-scoped binding. the TTL change made the fallback stick long enough to populate caches.

alice: tentative root cause: peering transient + rollout TTL semantics + region-scoped auth cache = compounded failure.

dana: immediate next steps i took: reverted TTL rollout -> rollback completed 1799004355. also left the temporary routing override in place until peering smoothing is implemented.

carlos: opened infra tickets INF-7421 (peering healthcheck smoothing + BGP dampening) and INF-7422 (auth: region-agnostic validation / coordinated cache invalidation).

ben: i've notified affected customers and closed their support tickets after confirmation. note for finance: some requests were metered against eu-edge during the window which will cause a small billing mismatch; looping in finance to reconcile.

alice: action items for postmortem: 1) timeline + logs (carlos) 2) revert confirmation (dana) 3) auth cache review (eng-auth + product) 4) add automated rollback guard for TTL-related rollouts (eng-platform). i'll start writeup in docs and tag product/support for billing check.

peering-bot: incident auto-closed 1799004387.
